title: Word: Copilot edits your document directly by default in chat
summary: The briefing passes: the default editing behaviour, published licence requirement and licence-assignment controls are supported. Searches found no dedicated tenant-wide switch for this default; the separate GCC roadmap item should be cited directly.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The release-note entry does not give the location of the user off switch.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Word turn off editing default; opened release-notes and read both occurrences of item 557673, including Details and Try this. Neither gives the off-switch location.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The release-note entry does not separately describe licence-specific rollout of the new chat default.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Word document editing default prerequisites 557673; read item 557673 in release-notes and the service description. The entry names no licence-specific rollout qualifications.

claims.claim: No additional Microsoft Learn page specifically documenting this new chat default was found beyond the release note.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot can edit your document by default in Word; Copilot Word document editing default prerequisites 557673; Copilot Word direct editing policy. Read release-notes, copilot-overview, requirements and service description; no separate page for this default found.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated an additional arrival step specific to this chat-default change.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Word document editing default prerequisites 557673; Copilot Word editing by default tenant policy admin switch. Read release-notes, requirements and admin settings; no extra activation step for item 557673 found.

claims.claim: The roadmap description concerns editing the document and describes no new data source.
claims.quote: The default chat experience with Copilot in Word now allows Copilot to directly edit your document.

claims.claim: Copilot uses existing Microsoft 365 data protection and access controls.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot works within the Microsoft 365 service boundary. It uses the same data protection, access control, and compliance capabilities that already apply across Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Copilot honours sensitivity labels when grounding responses and generating content.
claims.quote: Copilot honors Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels and encryption when it grounds responses and generates content.

claims.claim: The release notes describe the edits within the user's Word interaction.
claims.quote: Ask Copilot to rewrite a paragraph and watch the edits appear directly in the document.

claims.claim: No separate identity for this direct-editing default is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Word Copilot edit identity service principal; Copilot Word direct edit identity user session. Read release-notes, requirements and data-protection architecture; audit-copilot search describes in-app user interactions, not a separate editing identity.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on users have the full Copilot experience in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users without the add-on can use Copilot capabilities in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote.
claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license but can use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Some Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) features have fair use limits.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) refers to users without the Copilot add-on license, but who have access to Copilot capabilities inside apps (for example, Word or Excel). It doesn't include full chat integration. Some features are subject to fair use limits.

claims.claim: Copilot Chat (Basic) users do not have this Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote app access.
claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license and don't have access to Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Chat experiences in Word vary with licence and tenant configuration.
claims.quote: Chat experiences in Microsoft 365 apps vary depending on your tenant configuration and license.

claims.claim: The licensing model is add-on.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses reaches user licence assignment.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns the selected licence.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: User licence assignment governs who holds the Copilot add-on licence and consequently the licence tier for Copilot in Word.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Licence assignment is not a switch between direct editing on and off.
claims.quote: When you use the Active users page to assign or unassign licenses, you assign or unassign users licenses to products.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and api; summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No dedicated tenant-wide admin UI or API switch for Word's direct-editing default is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Word direct editing default disable tenant admin policy; Copilot Word editing by default tenant policy admin switch. Read configure-copilot-admin-center, copilotPolicySetting and release-notes. No dedicated editing-default switch found.

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings is where Microsoft lists Copilot settings.
claims.quote: As an administrator, you can manage many Microsoft Copilot settings from Copilot > Settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Graph copilotPolicySetting API is in preview.
claims.quote: This API is currently in preview.

claims.claim: The copilotPolicySetting page lists five supported settings, none specifically for Word editing.
claims.quote: Pin Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat; Block Copilot Access to Open Content; Control access to Designer Image Generation; Allow web search in Copilot; Control Admin Copilot availability in Microsoft 365 Admin Center

claims.claim: No separate licence specific to this change of default, beyond the published Edit with Copilot licence requirement, is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Word document editing default prerequisites 557673. Read service description, copilot-overview, requirements and release-notes; they publish the Copilot licence for Edit with Copilot, not another licence for the new chat default.
